narrative:
**Engagement pulled back sharply week-over-week while the 4-week trend stayed positive.** Model downloads fell 56.2% to 2,512,112 (from roughly 5.73M the prior week) across 24,237 tracked models, yet still sat 19.6% above the 4-week-ago level. Model likes fell 27.7% to 9,152 (from roughly 12,700), also up 8.8% on a 4-week basis, and Space likes dropped 75.9% to 610 (from roughly 2,530) against 6,874 tracked Spaces, while remaining 33.9% above four weeks ago. The uniform direction and magnitude of the one-week declines across three independent engagement metrics is more consistent with a collection or calendar artifact than with a genuine demand collapse; the positive 4-week deltas argue against reading this as a trend break. No 12-week comparisons were available in this cut.

**Qwen was the only model family to grow in absolute terms.** Qwen rose 7.2% to 4,986 models, while llama fell 14.5% to 812, nvidia-nemotron fell 42.2% to 115, deepseek fell 21.4% to 169, glm-zhipu fell 51.1% to 67, mistral fell 16.8% to 109, and gemma held roughly steady at 573 (-3.7%); other-open was flat at 5,639 (+0.2%) and kimi-moonshot rose to 67 (+123.3%). An important caveat: 11,700 of 24,237 models (48.3%) were unclassified as "unknown," down 6.7% week-over-week, so family-level shares should be treated as directional only. Within use cases that have usable sample sizes, Qwen held 26.1% of chat-assistant (n=664, +3.6%) and 36.0% of coding (n=139, -20.4%), and climbed to 16.0% of document-ai (n=187, +91.0%). Proprietary-API share slipped in both chat-assistant (11.0%, -11.0%) and coding (4.3%, -27.2%). For 3d-gaming (n=32), education (n=43), "other" (n=39), music-generation (n=19) and robotics (n=15), per-family counts implied by the shares were too few to report reliably despite large printed percentages.

**On the Spaces side, composition shifted toward scientific and vision/tool-centric work.** Scientific-tools Spaces rose 18.3% to 272 and "other" rose 3.9% to 2,071, while every other category declined — document-ai -18.7% to 443, search-research -12.1% to 385, education -9.8% to 222, chat-assistant -6.0% to 1,057, and music-generation -26.4% to 53. By SDK, static (3,950, -2.9%) and gradio (2,198, -0.9%) held roughly steady, whereas docker fell 14.7% to 607 and streamlit fell 23.8% to 64. Technology penetration showed vision-language at 7.24% (+14.5%) and tool-use at 3.61% (+14.6%), against declines in long-context (0.26%, -33.2%) and RAG (1.96%, -17.4%); agentic was essentially flat at 7.11%. Among verticals, legal (1.12%, +17.7%), e-commerce/retail (4.79%, +14.8%), industrial-manufacturing (3.27%, +11.9%) and healthcare (4.10%, +10.2%) gained, while cybersecurity (2.05%, -18.1%) and enterprise-productivity (6.71%, -7.3%) lost ground. Next week, watch whether engagement reverts toward the prior ~5.7M download level — confirming this week as an artifact — and whether Qwen's model-count gain and the scientific-tools Space build-out persist.
